Nintendo have a fucking huge mountain to climb, i.e. I expect zero miracles for Nintendo.

The Wii U was a freaking disaster.

Nintendo has released the Wii, Wii U, DS and variants, 3DS and variants, all heavily underpowered compared to their competition. And they just don't seem to 'get it' lately. Maybe they'll surprise us, but I don't have hopes that the NX will surpass even the Xbone in power.

There's nothing to "get." Nintendo has tried competing head on in terms of console power, and it gotten them the N64 and the fucking GameCube: terrible third party support (with endless, meaningless excuses as to why, such as the self-fulfilling prophecy, "nobody buys third party games on Nintendo consoles"), leaving a console propped up exclusively by first party software. Third parties have simply decided Nintendo consoles are anathema no matter how well they sell. But Nintendo handhelds are another issue entirely because reasons.

The PS1 was far less powerful than the N64, but that didn't help Nintendo. The GameCube was significantly more powerful than the PS2. That didn't help Nintendo. Why would a more powerful and more expensive NX help Nintendo at a time when the console business is contracting? Keep in mind Nintendo can't use money from another business division to subsidize hardware they lose money on producing like MS and Sony can (and do).

But it's a different era now. Xbone and PS4 are both x86, just make the NX x86, and even if it's a bit underpowered, as long as they produce the right dev tools making it easy to dev for, ports will come and they'll be a lot friendlier with third parties. As it is now, the hardware is weak, it's a pain to develop for, it has weird requirements (gamepad and backwards online), and the install base is already pathetically low given the time it's been on market. Fix those problems, release a new console, fix third party relations by supporting ports, then they can differentiate with their (excellent) first party games. They don't need to keep shoving in an overclocked gamecube into their 2016+ console.

The gamepad being an obstacle instead of an opportunity truly speaks to the laziness and unimaginative nature of most developers, just as their tepid use of the Wiimote and, to a lesser degree, the DS's second screen did. "Port and forget!"

The online is a real problem, though. I know Nintendo isn't a technology company the way Sony and Microsoft are, but they really need to get their shit together. It's better than the abysmal Wii online, but not by much. (They have a unique problem of being attacked every time something that isn't kid-friendly happens in their games or online services, but still.)

The GameCube architecture needs to be fucking retired, yes. The 3DS is the last time they can get away with that.

I don't believe just having an equally powerful console will fix their third party problems, though. It should. But it won't.
